description: Long low hall with an open colonnaded front sheltering a gilded Buddha figure lying on its side, the figure visible the length of the opening.

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Long low rectangular hall under a shallow two-tier tiled roof, one long side open as a colonnade of square pillars with no wall between them, a very long gilded Buddha figure lying on its side on a low plinth running the full interior length, head propped on one hand at the near end and feet squared off at the far end, low stepped platform along the open front Materials: Gold-leafed figure with worn patches showing dark lacquer beneath, red and gold roof tiles, whitewashed pillars stained at the base, dusty stone plinth, soot darkening on the ceiling above.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.91, up from 0.86. The second build had the right envelope and the right roof FORM; what it lacked was read off the proxy's own elevations and a 2x zoom of the plate: a taller colonnade (5.45 m against 4.85), a narrower and longer hall (band table 0.074 / 0.079 -> 0.025 / 0.027), a 13.5 m ridge, a wall-pier at the head end with seven columns instead of a twelve-column peristyle, a figure a quarter larger in section on a low plinth, and the wear that is this plate's identity at prop distance -- black column feet, scalloped courses, tarnished gilt, a smoke-stained interior -- as four post-construction canvases over five textureless materials. Remaining drag is the figure's unauthored surface (robe folds, face, soles) and lightingCamera 0.84 on a plate whose subject is in shade. 3,244/32,000 triangles, 8/24 draw calls, 5/16 materials, 8/32 unique geometries, 4 canvases at 5.3 MB, factory ~70 ms.

featureReviews.evidence: A 15.9 m figure on its RIGHT side facing the colonnade, head at +Z in the bay beside the wall-pier: one smooth 32-segment body from neck to ankle, taller than deep, the upper leg a soft ridge on it, stacked feet with a toe comb, an upright tilted head with ushnisha and ear lobes cupped in the right hand, the forearm near-vertical from an elbow on the plinth, the left arm along the flank to a hand on the thigh. Its body top sits at 4.2 m -- half the column height -- which is where the plate's 2x colonnade zoom puts it, and its gilt is mottled with tarnish.
featureReviews.notes: The second build's figure reached 3.3 m in a hall whose columns now run to 6.95: it lay too small in its own hall and read as a pipe between columns. Section scaled 1.25 about the figure's rest line (so every station still rests on the plinth), length 0.72 of the authored stations, plinth lowered to 2.30 on two 0.40 m steps as the plate shows a low three-step plinth rather than a 0.87 m block. The tarnish is what the plate actually shows on the gilt -- dark mottled patches -- delivered as six jagged polygons per 3 m tile after nine at 0.85 alpha read as a leopard. Still unauthored: robe folds, hairline, face, sole marks; the plate shows the figure in shade behind columns, which is thin evidence for any of them.

featureReviews.evidence: Seven square columns 5.45 m tall along the open front, a 2.45 m wall-pier closing the head end's front corner, one mid column at each end; black grime at every column base from a 6 m stone tile phase-locked to the column foot; the figure legible through the bays along its length with a smoke-stained interior face behind at luma 82+.
featureReviews.notes: The second build's twelve equal columns from 1.75 to 6.60 were a peristyle the plate does not have. The count, the pier and the open feet end are read off a 2x zoom of the plate's colonnade (scratch/_bud/front_zoom.png); the column height off the proxy's orthographic side elevation (columns 1.5 -> 6.95, lower eaves 7.05). The grime tile is phase-locked so its band lands at the column base and the wall foot; the first pass wrapped that band onto the wall's TOP edge (a 5.45 tile on a 5.45 wall) and onto the terrace deck, fixed by a 6 m tile and by mapping horizontal faces into the tile's clean middle rows.

featureReviews.evidence: Two HIPPED tiers -- lower at pitch 0.64 from eaves at 7.05, upper at 0.50 from 8.30 to an apex at 9.80 -- with ridgeHalfZ authored per tier (5.60 / 6.75) so the ridge runs 0.70 of the eaves length and the end hips are steeper than the sides, as the proxy elevations measure; a three-course ochre border at each eaves, scalloped fish-scale tile courses in running bond over both, grey capped ribs chained down every hip and a cap on each ridge.
featureReviews.notes: The second build's hip had ridgeHalfZ = hz - hx (equal pitch on both axes), which gave a 4.5 m ridge where the proxy side elevation shows 13.5 m at y=10 and the upper eaves at 17.1 m -- band 9 read -0.09 in depth. Its 0.34 m border on a short slope also read as stripes; 0.30 of rise is three courses as the plate lays them. The red is authored a step more saturated than measured (#B25A4B against #A9695F) because ACES desaturated the as-measured slope to pink, the ubosot's lesson; the course tile re-bases both roof materials by its own 0.93 mean at bind time.

featureReviews.evidence: Five materials at PBR confidence 0.822-0.860 under four post-construction multiplier tiles: stone grime (soft drift, grain, washes, a base band), fish-scale courses on tile and border, gilt tarnish, smoke on the interior. Each authored albedo is the measurement divided by its tile's mean, recorded on the material.
featureReviews.notes: The second build was textureless throughout and rendered as flat paint; the plate's identity at this distance is precisely its wear -- the black column feet, the scalloped courses, the tarnished gilt. Delivered the way every weathered hero prop in this kit is: seeded Canvas 2D tiles bound after construction as map and bump, so the sculpt materials stay textureless and no material is added. 512 px, ~70 ms, 5.3 MB of texture VRAM.

name: Reclining Buddha Hall
nameTh: วิหารพระนอน
notes:
The reclining figure is modelled as part of this asset rather than as a separate statue, and the long front is open colonnade rather than a wall, because the two decisions depend on each other: a closed long low box has no recognisable feature at all and would read as a warehouse, and the whole identity of the building is the gilded figure seen lengthwise through the opening. That means this asset is a building and a large statue together and its material budget has to cover both gold leaf and roofing. No destruction groups: it is static landmark geometry.

SIZE CORRECTED 2026-08-31 from 14.0 x 10.0 x 28.0. The 28 m was a list-time estimate reasoned from the figure ('the figure alone sets the minimum length') and never checked, because Meshy refuses this plate with a content_policy_violation and the safety checker is forced on -- so this was the only prop in the kit whose proportions had never been checked band by band, and its silhouette layer was carried at 0.72 for exactly that reason. Meshy is not the only image-to-3d: fal-ai/trellis and fal-ai/hunyuan3d/v2 both accept the plate. They read length/height 1.852 and 2.020 and width/height 1.226 and 1.265 -- agreeing with each other to 8.7% and 3.2%, and disagreeing with the build's 2.818 and 1.410 by 46% and 13%. Height is the anchor and does not move: the proxies give ratios only, and the vertical breakdown was already right (the proxy end elevation puts the roof at 31% of total height against the build's 32%). At h 10.0 the mean gives d 19.24 and w 12.38. The band table then goes from mean |delta depth| 0.7267 to 0.0789 and |delta width| 0.1312 to 0.0739.

The plate cannot arbitrate this, and that is measured rather than assumed: a projective solve needs edges that are parallel in plan to be parallel in the image, and fitting the platform's ground silhouette gives four clean straight runs whose two must-be-parallel pairs differ in image slope by 47% and 34%. No single camera projects that -- the plate is a generated image and its perspective is only locally consistent. Do not re-attempt the solve here. The known proxy bias runs with the correction rather than against it: single-view reconstructions inflate depth, so if these two are wrong the true hall is shorter still, and 19.24 m is a floor.
